title: Schema-agnostic structured-log hydrator: session fingerprint & privacy gating
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add an edge-side, schema-agnostic 'hydrator' that normalizes incoming structured logs into a compact canonical envelope, emits a deterministic session fingerprint (sliding-window anchor-based) for cross-service correlation, and applies tenant-configurable privacy gating (PII scrubbing, token redaction, and sample-based retention tiers). Goal is to increase reliability of cross-host joins while reducing index cardinality and protecting customer PII at ingest time.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Hydrator can accept JSON/ndjson/protobuf envelopes and output canonical envelope with 'session_fingerprint' and 'canonical_ts'.
2) Deterministic fingerprint matches across retries and modest clock skew (unit tests +/- 2s tolerance).
3) Privacy gating rules allow per-tenant regex redaction and field-level hashing; redaction rules configurable via tenant config service.
4) End-to-end pipeline ingest rate maintains >= 85% of baseline at 95th percentile CPU/memory for edge sidecar.
5) New fields are backwards-compatible (old consumers ignore unknown fields).
6) Observability: Grafana dashboard shows fingerprint cardinality, scrubbed-field counts, PII redaction rate, and added latency histogram.
7) E2E test against staging Loki demonstrates reduced label cardinality by >= 30% on synthetic high-cardinality stream.
design_notes:
High-level approach:
- Hydrator runs as an optional sidecar or ingress lambda before the existing Loki/ELK forwarder.
- Use schema-agnostic projection: probe top-level keys and nested maps to locate candidate request/session keys (user_id, session_id, trace_id, cookie, anon_id). Do not rely on a fixed ontology.
- Session fingerprint: compute ordered mini-hash over up to N anchors (timestamped event keys) in a sliding 30s window. Hash algorithm: XXH3 128-bit truncated to 64bits, then base62 encode to short token. This yields stable token even when some anchors missing.
- Privacy gating: tenants can supply scrub rules (regex, keep-first/last, token-hash). Apply redaction before fingerprint calculation for fields marked PII. Provide sampled retention tiers (hot/standard/cold) that tag messages for downstream retention policies.
- Backpressure & perf: implement fast-path no-op for messages that already match canonical envelope version. Use zero-copy JSON scanning (simdjson) where available and fall back to a lightweight Go decoder.
- Compatibility: preserve original raw payload in compressed 'raw_blob' only when tenant config allows retention. By default store only canonical envelope.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): deploy hydrator sidecar to 3 low-traffic tenants for 72h, monitor CPU, memory, and added p50/p95 ingest latency.
Phase 2 (shadow): run hydrator in shadow mode for 10% of incoming traffic in the eu-west region for 7 days; compare fingerprint cardinality and false-positive correlation rate against control.
Phase 3 (opt-in): enable for customers who opt in and for internal prod-only tenants.
Phase 4 (global): enable default behavior with conservative privacy gating and hook into retention pipeline.
Rollback strategy: toggle off by configuration flag at gateway; fall back to raw forwarder instantly.
Communication: update changelog, release notes, and add docs/confluence page with sample scrub rules and onboarding checklist.
test_plan:
Unit tests for anchor selection, fingerprint stability, and redaction logic with fuzzed inputs.
Integration tests: ingest pipeline against staging Loki index verifying cardinality and label size.
Performance tests: synthetic load to measure p50/p95 latency impact and CPU/memory delta vs baseline.
Security tests: run static analysis and privacy fuzzing (random PII injection) to ensure redaction cannot be bypassed.
Canary monitoring: create Grafana alerts for >5% increase in ingest latency or >2x growth in label cardinality in canary tenants.

2026-02-25 - Diego Morales: Implemented prototype in sidecar-go branch. Initial perf numbers look promising (p50 +2ms at 1000rps). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/5421

2026-03-05 - Priya Gupta: Security review requested. Need to confirm KMS usage for deterministic hashing salt storage and tenant ACLs for scrub-rule editing.
2026-03-09 - Diego Morales: Addressed salt storage — using tenant-scoped KMS key ring and a read-only salt API. Added rotation plan in security notes.
2026-03-12 - Asha Patel: Canary scheduled for 2026-03-15 in infra cycle. Added dependabot note for simdjson native bindings update.
security_notes: Deterministic fingerprint uses tenant-specific salt stored in KMS; salts are rotated quarterly. Redaction rules evaluated in a whitelist-first manner to avoid over-redaction. Log training/heuristics run only on scrubbed examples; raw_blob preservation disabled by default to reduce PII risk. Security review flagged need for explicit audit log when scrub rules change (added).
open_questions:
1) Should session_fingerprint be exposed as a top-level Loki label by default or kept as a field to avoid label explosion?
2) How aggressive should default scrub rules be for marketplaces with multi-tenant IDs embedded in headers?
3) Is XXH3 acceptable for collision risk with our retention window, or switch to SipHash/HMAC for higher guarantees?
notes_for_ops: Add new metrics: hydrator.processed_total, hydrator.scrubbed_fields_total, hydrator.fingerprint_cardinality_estimate, hydrator.latency_seconds_bucket. Expose internal health endpoint and a lightweight /metrics shard-friendly collector. Ensure sidecar config hot-reloads scrub rules without restart.
